prompt.adult: After the letters to the churches, John looked and saw something standing open in heaven. Then a voice like a trumpet said, "Come up here." What did he see?
prompt.child: John looked up and saw something standing open in heaven, and a voice that sounded like a trumpet called him to come up. What did he see standing open?
prompt.teen: Revelation 4:1 begins a new vision. What did John see standing open in heaven?
prompt.older: According to Revelation 4:1, what did John behold standing open in heaven?

verses.text: After these things I looked, and behold, a door standing open in heaven. And the first voice which I heard was like a trumpet speaking with me, saying, “Come up here, and I will show you things which must take place after this.”

explanation.adult: Read the first sentence of Revelation 4:1, right after "and behold."
explanation.child: Look at the start of Revelation 4:1. What John saw comes right after "behold."
explanation.teen: 4:1 has two parts: what John saw and what the voice said. Read the first part.
explanation.older: The object of John's sight follows "behold" in the opening sentence of 4:1.

teaching.extended_explanation: Revelation 4 opens a new scene after the seven letters. John sees something in heaven, and a voice like a trumpet invites him to come up and be shown what must take place. Read the first sentence of 4:1.
teaching.takeaway: John saw a door standing open in heaven.

review.notes: Growing stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _growing_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: John saw a throne set in heaven, and One sat on it. What was around the throne, in appearance like an emerald?
prompt.child: In heaven John saw Someone sitting on a throne. Something green like an emerald circled the throne. What was it?
prompt.teen: Revelation 4:3 describes the One on the throne and something around the throne. What was around it, like an emerald?
prompt.older: According to Revelation 4:3, what surrounded the throne, in appearance like an emerald?

verses.text: Immediately I was in the Spirit; and behold, a throne set in heaven, and One sat on the throne.
And He who sat there was like a jasper and a sardius stone in appearance; and there was a rainbow around the throne, in appearance like an emerald.

explanation.adult: Read the second half of Revelation 4:3, right after "and there was."
explanation.child: Look at Revelation 4:3 after the stones are named. It says what was around the throne.
explanation.teen: 4:3 first describes the One seated, then what surrounded the throne. Read the second part.
explanation.older: The second clause of 4:3, after "and there was," names what encircled the throne.

teaching.extended_explanation: In 4:2, John sees a throne in heaven with One seated on it. Verse 3 describes Him with precious stones and then tells what was around the throne, comparing its look to an emerald. Read the second half of 4:3.
teaching.takeaway: There was a rainbow around the throne, like an emerald.

review.notes: Growing stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _growing_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: The four living creatures, each with six wings, do not rest day or night from their song. After calling Him "Lord God Almighty," how does their song describe Him?
prompt.child: Four living creatures in heaven never stop praising God, day or night. After they call Him Lord God Almighty, what do they say about Him?
prompt.teen: Revelation 4:8 records the song of the four living creatures. After "Lord God Almighty," what is the last line?
prompt.older: According to Revelation 4:8, how do the living creatures describe the Lord God Almighty at the close of their song?

choices.text: Who rides on the clouds of heaven
Who was and is and is to come

verses.text: The four living creatures, each having six wings, were full of eyes around and within. And they do not rest day or night, saying: “Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, Who was and is and is to come!”

explanation.adult: Read the very end of the song in Revelation 4:8, right after "Lord God Almighty."
explanation.child: Look at the last words of Revelation 4:8. They come right after "Lord God Almighty."
explanation.teen: The song in 4:8 has three parts. Read the last one, after "Lord God Almighty."
explanation.older: The closing line of the creatures' song in 4:8 follows "Lord God Almighty."

teaching.extended_explanation: The four living creatures are full of eyes and never stop worshiping. Their song begins by praising God's holiness, then names Him Lord God Almighty, and ends with one more line. Read the last line of 4:8.
teaching.takeaway: The living creatures sing of the Lord God Almighty, "Who was and is and is to come!"

review.notes: Growing stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _growing_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: The twenty-four elders fall down before Him who sits on the throne and cast their crowns before it. What reason do they give that He is worthy to receive glory and honor and power?
prompt.child: The elders in heaven bow down and throw their crowns in front of the throne. They say God is worthy of glory and honor and power. Why do they say He is worthy?
prompt.teen: In Revelation 4:11, the elders say why God is worthy of glory, honor, and power. What reason do they give?
prompt.older: According to Revelation 4:11, on what ground do the elders declare Him worthy?

choices.text: You gave the law to Moses

verses.text: the twenty-four elders fall down before Him who sits on the throne and worship Him who lives forever and ever, and cast their crowns before the throne, saying:
“You are worthy, O Lord, To receive glory and honor and power; For You created all things, And by Your will they exist and were created.”

explanation.adult: Read the second half of the elders' words in Revelation 4:11, right after "For."
explanation.child: Look at Revelation 4:11. The reason starts with the word "For."
explanation.teen: 4:10 shows what the elders do; 4:11 gives their words. Read the part that begins with "For."
explanation.older: The ground of His worthiness is the clause introduced by "For" in 4:11.

teaching.extended_explanation: Whenever the living creatures give glory to God, the elders fall down, worship, and lay their crowns before the throne. Their song in 4:11 says He is worthy and then gives the reason. Read the part that begins with "For."
teaching.takeaway: The elders say He is worthy, "for You created all things."

review.notes: Growing stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _growing_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: When the scroll had been taken, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down, each with a harp and golden bowls full of incense. What does Revelation 5:8 say the incense is?
prompt.child: The elders and living creatures each held a harp and golden bowls full of incense. Revelation 5:8 tells what that incense stands for. What is it?
prompt.teen: Revelation 5:8 explains the golden bowls of incense. What are they?
prompt.older: According to Revelation 5:8, what is the incense in the golden bowls?

verses.text: Now when He had taken the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb, each having a harp, and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.

explanation.adult: Read the end of Revelation 5:8, right after "which are."
explanation.child: Look at the last words of Revelation 5:8. They tell what the incense is.
explanation.teen: 5:8 describes the harps and bowls, then explains the incense. Read what follows "which are."
explanation.older: The meaning of the incense is given in the words that close 5:8, after "which are."

teaching.extended_explanation: In 5:8, the living creatures and elders fall down in worship, holding harps and golden bowls full of incense. The verse does not leave the incense unexplained; it says what it is. Read the words after "which are."
teaching.takeaway: The incense is the prayers of the saints.

review.notes: Growing stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _growing_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: One of the elders told John to stop weeping. When John looked, what did he see standing in the midst of the throne and the four living creatures, which then took the scroll?
prompt.child: John was crying because no one could open the scroll. Then an elder told him not to weep. John looked, and someone stood near the throne and took the scroll. What did John see?
prompt.teen: In Revelation 5:6-7, John looks and sees who stands in the midst of the throne and takes the scroll. What does he see?
prompt.older: According to Revelation 5:6, what did John behold standing in the midst of the throne and the elders?

verses.text: And I looked, and behold, in the midst of the throne and of the four living creatures, and in the midst of the elders, stood a Lamb as though it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven Spirits of God sent out into all the earth.
Then He came and took the scroll out of the right hand of Him who sat on the throne.

explanation.adult: Read the middle of Revelation 5:6, right after "in the midst of the elders, stood."
explanation.child: Look at Revelation 5:6. What John saw comes right after the word "stood."
explanation.teen: 5:6 tells where John looked and what stood there; 5:7 shows it taking the scroll. Read the word after "stood."
explanation.older: What John beheld is named right after "stood" in 5:6, before the seven horns and seven eyes.

teaching.extended_explanation: John had wept because no one was found able to open the scroll. When he looked again, he saw who stood at the center of the throne, the living creatures, and the elders, with seven horns and seven eyes. In 5:7 He takes the scroll. Read the words right after "stood" in 5:6.
teaching.takeaway: John saw a Lamb standing in the midst of the throne.

review.notes: Growing stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _growing_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: In Revelation 5:4, John wept much because no one was found worthy to open the scroll. In the new song of 5:9, what reason is given that the One who took the scroll is worthy?
prompt.child: John cried because nobody was worthy to open the scroll. Later, a new song says Someone is worthy to take it. What reason does the song give?
prompt.teen: 5:4 says no one was worthy; 5:9 says One is. What reason does the new song give for His worthiness?
prompt.older: Contrasting Revelation 5:4 with the new song of 5:9, on what ground is the One who took the scroll declared worthy?

verses.text: So I wept much, because no one was found worthy to open and read the scroll, or to look at it.

And they sang a new song, saying: “You are worthy to take the scroll, And to open its seals; For You were slain, And have redeemed us to God by Your blood Out of every tribe and tongue and people and nation,

explanation.adult: Read the new song in Revelation 5:9, right after "For."
explanation.child: Look at Revelation 5:9. The reason in the song starts with the word "For."
explanation.teen: 5:4 is the problem; 5:9 is the answer in song. Read the words after "For" in 5:9.
explanation.older: The ground of worthiness in 5:9 is the clause introduced by "For," before "And have redeemed us."

teaching.extended_explanation: At first no one in heaven or on earth could open the scroll, and John wept (5:3-4). Then the living creatures and elders sang a new song saying the One who took the scroll is worthy, and they gave a reason, followed by what He did for people of every tribe and tongue. Read the words after "For" in 5:9.
teaching.takeaway: The new song says He is worthy, "For You were slain."

review.notes: Growing stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _growing_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: Countless angels, and then every creature in heaven, on earth, under the earth, and in the sea, joined the praise (Revelation 5:12-13). How did the four living creatures respond in 5:14?
prompt.child: First many angels praised loudly, and then every creature everywhere joined in. When all that praise was done, what did the four living creatures say?
prompt.teen: 5:12-13 build the praise from angels to every creature. What one word do the four living creatures say in 5:14?
prompt.older: Following the widening praise of Revelation 5:12-13, what did the four living creatures say in 5:14?

verses.text: saying with a loud voice: “Worthy is the Lamb who was slain To receive power and riches and wisdom, And strength and honor and glory and blessing!”

And every creature which is in heaven and on the earth and under the earth and such as are in the sea, and all that are in them, I heard saying: “Blessing and honor and glory and power Be to Him who sits on the throne, And to the Lamb, forever and ever!”
Then the four living creatures said, “Amen!” And the twenty-four elders fell down and worshiped Him who lives forever and ever.

explanation.adult: Read the beginning of Revelation 5:14, right after "the four living creatures said."
explanation.child: Look at the start of Revelation 5:14. The living creatures say one word.
explanation.teen: 5:12 is the angels; 5:13 is every creature. Read what the living creatures say at the start of 5:14.
explanation.older: The creatures' reply is the single word quoted at the opening of 5:14.

teaching.extended_explanation: The praise in Revelation 5 spreads wider and wider: first the living creatures and elders, then ten thousand times ten thousand angels (5:11-12), then every creature everywhere (5:13). The chapter ends with a one-word reply from the four living creatures and the elders falling down in worship. Read the start of 5:14.
